instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and line two baking sheets with parchment.

Put the mochiko, cooked rice, salt and oil in a food processor and pulse until the mix looks coarse. Add 1/4 cup of water slowly while it runs. If you have no food processor, mash the rice into the flour and oil with a fork, then work in the water.
Transfer the dough to a bowl and press it until it holds together. Roll golf-ball-sized pieces, flatten each between two sheets of parchment to about 1/8 inch thick and cut out circles.
Lay the circles on the baking sheets. Bake for 10 minutes, flip them and bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until they're golden and crisp.
Stir the soy sauce and mirin in a small bowl. Brush both sides of each cracker and sprinkle with the black and white sesame seeds. Bake for 3 to 4 minutes, until the glaze is set and darker.
Cool the crackers completely on a rack. They crisp up as they cool.
Serve once cool. Keep leftovers in a closed container for a few days.
method_notes: The one published recipe found by name bakes a dough of mochiko, cooked rice, oil and water, then brushes the crackers with a soy and mirin glaze and bakes them again. Other versions fry or grill the crackers and glaze with soy sauce and sugar. The lead also mixes furikake into the dough; that is left out here because many furikake blends contain bonito, and this has to stay vegan. Only one unrated source could be read, so amounts follow it closely.
